result.title: CompoSET: A Controlled Single-Edit Benchmark for Vision-Language Compositionality
result.comment: Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/CompoSET/CompoSET | Code: https://github.com/laure-delisle/CompoSET | 9 pages main text, 38 pages total
result.summary: Vision-language compositionality is the ability to identify which properties, relations, quantities, and states bind to which entities in both an image and a caption, and to match those bindings across modalities. Existing benchmarks evaluate this ability through image-text matching: a model ranks candidate image-caption match similarities and succeeds when the correct match comes on top. In such datasets, paired images differ by more than a single binding: scene, layout, and content all differ, with 97% of pixels changing on average. Such pairs do not isolate compositionality: results are confounded by global image differences. We introduce Compositional Single-EdiT (CompoSET), a benchmark dataset in which each base image-caption pair has an edited counterpart, or foil, that preserves the scene but differs by a single controlled edit, such as color, count, spatial relation, or object state. Base and foil images preserve naturalistic scene complexity yet are visually near-identical: only 8% of pixels change on average. Our dataset has many foils per base scene (~22) in order to separate scene difficulty from edit difficulty, a distinction one-foil-per-base benchmarks cannot make. CompoSET contains 1,776 instances across 80 naturalistic scenes, spanning 16 edit types in 4 semantic categories, with captions at 3 verbosity levels. We test 22 dual-encoder VLMs and find that all models perform at or below chance level on CompoSET, despite scoring well on prior benchmarks. This suggests that apparent progress under prior image-text matching protocols may be an artifact arising from confounds in benchmark design, and that compositional understanding in dual-encoder VLMs is far from solved. CompoSET addresses the confounds and offers a better controlled benchmark to measure future progress.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CompoSET 基准：每个图像-文本对配一个仅做单一受控编辑（颜色、数量、空间关系、物体状态等）的 foil，像素变化约 8%，覆盖 80 个场景、16 类编辑，并测试 22 个双编码器 VLM。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接诊断「属性/关系绑定到哪个实体」这一视觉细节与实体关系保留问题，并指出旧基准的全局差异混淆使模型分数虚高；可供核查 LVR 内部状态是否真正保留任务必要的绑定信息，但其评测仍是图文匹配而非 latent 推理过程。
